title: The Weight of a Word
logline: A family finds an old cassette recording of a relative who has died, and gathers to hear a voice that sounds exactly the same as it always did.
human_question: A recording can keep a voice. What does it lose?

premise.story: A family decides, in its own time, whether and when to listen again to an old recording, told entirely through their own choice and reactions.
premise.place: A family home, wherever the tape and a working player happen to be.
premise.experience: The search for a machine that still plays, the first seconds of a familiar voice, and the strange gap between hearing someone and them being there.

concept_links.why: The source notices precisely this: a machine can reproduce the sound of someone's voice exactly, and yet what made the sound a message, a living person's intention shaping breath and throat at that moment, is missing. It gives that absence a name.
The wider inventory of matter that includes sound as a conditioned, momentary thing frames why a recording can copy the sound but not renew the person who once produced it.

what_camera_could_observe: Finding the tape, or a box of old recordings, while clearing a shelf
Searching for a player that still works
The first seconds of the voice, and faces in the room
Someone speaking back to the recording, or staying silent
The tape put away again, wherever the family decides it belongs
what_must_be_real: The family's own grief, timing and choice. Nothing staged, repeated for the camera, or scheduled to suit a shoot; the family decides whether this is filmed at all, and can stop at any point.

possible_arc.opening: A box of tapes found, half by accident.
possible_arc.turn: The voice starts, and the room changes.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the family actually does next.

requirements: A family with an old recording of a relative who has died, willing to be filmed on their own terms
No pressure or scheduling that would turn grief into a performance
Full control by the family over what is filmed and used

risks: Grief must not be staged, prolonged or repeated for the camera
The family, not a schedule, decides whether and when this happens
Risk of turning a private moment into spectacle
drop_if: No family willing to have this moment filmed on their own terms
The presence of a camera would itself change or intrude on the moment

connections.note: A voice a machine can copy but not mean; a limb a workshop can make but cannot, by itself, make someone's own.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
